docs:
Evolution Changes

Pokémon that would normally need to be traded to evolve now have an additional evolution
method. As a quick summary, Pokémon that don’t need to hold an item when traded will
evolve via happiness, while those that do need an item will evolve by levelling up while
holding that item.

Also, please note that not all Rockruff can evolve into Dusk Lycanroc; only the ones with
Own Tempo can do this, and they must have the ability when they are caught (you can’t get it
with an ability capsule).

All changes are as follows:

    • Eevee => Glaceon: Use an Ice Stone
    • Eevee => Leafeon: Use a Leaf Stone
    • Graveler => Golem: level up with high happiness
    • Kadabra => Alakazam: level up with high happiness
    • Machoke => Machamp: level up with high happiness
    • Haunter => Gengar: level up with high happiness
    • Onix => Steelix: level up holding a Metal Coat
    • Scyther => Scizor: level up holding a Metal Coat
    • Seadra => Kingdra: level up holding a Dragon Scale
    • Poliwhirl => Politoed: level up holding a King’s Rock
    • Slowpoke => Slowking: level up holding a King’s Rock
    • Porygon => Porygon2: level up holding an Up-Grade
    • Porygon2 => Porygon-Z: level up holding a Dubious Disc
    • Clamperl => Huntail: level up holding a Deep Sea Tooth
    • Clamperl => Gorebyss: level up holding a Deep Sea Scale
    • Dusclops => Dusknoir: level up holding a Reaper Cloth
    • Magmar => Magmortar: level up holding a Magmarizer
    • Electabuzz => Electivire: level up holding an Electirizer
    • Rhydon => Rhyperior: level up holding a Protector
    • Feebas => Milotic: level up holding a Prism Scale
    • Karrablast => Escavalier: level up with a Shelmet in the party
    • Shelmet => Accelgor: level up with a Karrablast in the party
    • Gurdurr => Conkeldurr: level up with high happiness
    • Boldore => Gigalith: level up with high happiness
    • Spritzee => Aromatisse: level up holding a Sachet
    • Swirlix => Slurpuff: level up holding a Whipped Dream
    • Phantump => Trevenant: level up with high happiness
    • Pumpkaboo => Gourgeist: level up with high happiness
    • Cosmoem => Solgaleo: level up in Ultra Moon starting at level 53
    • Cosmoem => Lunala: level up in Ultra Sun starting at level 53
    • Rockruff => Lycanroc Midday: level up during the day starting at level 25
    • Rockruff => Lycanroc Midnight: level up during the night starting at level 25
    • Magneton => Magnezone: Use a Thunder Stone
    • Nosepass => Probopass: Use a Thunder Stone
    • Charjabug => Vikavolt: Use a Thunder Stone (Standard versions only)

    • Crabrawler => Crabominable: Use an Ice Stone

Additionally, the following Pokémon will evolve at lower levels:

    • Snorunt 42 => 30
    • Vanillite 35 => 25
    • Vanillish 47 => 37
    • Tynamo 39 => 20
    • Rufflet 54 => 34
    • Vullaby 54 => 34
    • Pawniard 52 => 42
    • Deino 50 => 40
    • Zweilous 64 => 54
    • Larvesta 59 => 49
    • Mienfoo 50 => 40
    • Klink 38 => 28
    • Klang 49 => 39
    • Skrelp 48 => 37
    • Noibat can now evolve when levelled up with high friendship at night.

Pokémon Type Changes

                     (Rebalanced Versions Only)

These are also listed in the Pokémon Changes document but are provided again here for quick
reference.

• Fearow: Normal/Flying => Dark/Flying
• Arbok: Poison => Poison/Dark
• Ninetales: Fire => Fire/Fairy
• Golduck: Water = Water/Psychic

Quick Guide: Early Access to
        Mega Evolutions

Because Mega Evolution is locked to the post game in Ultra Sun & Ultra Moon, you may want
to use a save editor to enable it earlier. The best time to do this is after defeating Guzma for the
first time (this is when enemy trainers will start using Megas), but you can do it whenever you
want. This guide will briefly explain how to do so.

                                      Step One

Get a copy of PKHeX from this link: https://projectpokemon.org/home/files/file/1-pkhex/

                                      Step Two

Run PKHeX.exe, click File => Open and navigate to your save file.
If you’re using Citra and don’t know where this is, right-click on your installed game and select
“Open Save Data Location” to find it.

You can then copy paste the save file path into the dialogue box that popped up, like so:

Then, select the file named “main” to open your save.
If you’re playing on a 3DS with CFW, you probably know how to dump your save files by
now. If not, get a program named JKSM and follow a guide on how to use it.

                                      Step Three

Click on the Trainer Info tab:

Then click navigate to the Misc tab:

Finally, check the “unlocked Mega Evolution” box and save.

                                     Step Four

Now you’ll need to give yourself the Mega Stone(s) you want. The easiest way to do this is to
edit a Pokémon’s held item to be the appropriate Mega Stone. If your party Pokémon are all
holding items, give it to any Pokémon in a box instead.

                                      Step Five

Finally, save your changes by selecting file => Export SAV => Export main and overwriting
your old save.

If you’re playing on 3DS, don’t forget to import your modified save afterwards!
